issues.description: overrideCount doubling from 6 to 12 with removed isParent guard is unexplained and may regress override semantics
issues.detail: The test 'override: do not run on references' had its expected count doubled after the !seen.isParent guard was dropped. Either overrides now fire on parent wrapper nodes (a behavior change for every override user) or this masks a regression. The PR offers no rationale and the test name still claims overrides do not run on references. Needs explicit justification or revert.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as structural equality test in dedup loops is slow and semantically fragile
issues.detail: finalize compares schema[key] to refSeen.def![key] via JSON.stringify round-trip twice. This is O(size) per key, order-sensitive, mishandles undefined/functions, and conflates structural equality with provenance. The real question is whether a property was inherited from parent vs child — that should be tracked at process-time, not re-derived from string shape. Use a real deepEqual or track origin.

issues.description: flattenRef has multiple overlapping dedup passes with unstated invariants and incidental termination
issues.detail: The function now has three nearly-identical dedup branches (isParentRef strip, refSchema.$ref stringify-dedup, seen.parent stringify-dedup) plus recursive flattenRef(seen.parent) calls. Termination relies on seen.ref=null as a single sentinel with no shared visited set across the parent recursion. Loop invariants are not stated; one general traversal of the inheritance chain would replace three special cases.

issues.description: ref and parent fields complect inheritance and lineage in one Seen record with mutation-as-sentinel
issues.detail: Seen now carries both ref (processor-set property inheritance) and parent (clone-chain lineage), entangled via precedence rules like isParentRef, seen.parent !== ref, and auto-fill if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent. Two distinct concerns are intertwined in one field with seen.ref=null mutation as termination signal. Decompose: keep parent purely as lineage, derive inheritance separately, and document the two roles.

issues.description: play.ts committed as scratch debug script with relative source import and console.logs
issues.detail: play.ts switched from importing zod/v4 to a relative path into packages/zod/src/index.js with console.log probes for the metadata bug. This is a debugging artifact, not a shipped example or test. It will rot and confuse readers treating top-level files as canonical. Delete it before merge or convert into a real test pinning the behavior.

issues.description: fileProcessor refactor is bundled with the metadata fix and should be split
issues.detail: The json-schema-processors.ts change hoisting shared string-schema props to the root and leaving only contentMediaType in each anyOf branch is unrelated to metadata/parent propagation. It is a clean simplification on its own merits but mixing it with the core fix prevents bisecting a regression in file emission against the metadata refactor. Split into a separate patch.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug — metadata and $ref propagation through wrapper chains like readonly().meta({id}).describe() — and the new test demonstrates the fix. However, the implementation entangles two concerns (property inheritance vs clone-chain lineage) in one Seen record, leans on JSON.stringify as a structural-equality oracle in three overlapping dedup loops, and silently changes override semantics (6→12 invocations with the isParent guard removed) without justification. Termination of the recursive flattenRef rests on a single mutation sentinel rather than a proven invariant. Before merge: explain the override-count doubling, replace stringify-based dedup with provenance tracking or a real deepEqual, split out the unrelated fileProcessor refactor, and drop the play.ts scratch file.
